anchors: add one arm that delivers the source document verbatim
decision: When the variants rewrite ideas taken from a source document, the grid gets one arm that delivers the source document verbatim, checked before seal.

evidence.text: 2026-11-05: after 17 arms the user noticed every variant was a rewrite of the note and none delivered it unchanged. GREEN opus and haiku added the arm; the reorder-only control got none.

reopen_if: The harness itself refuses or warns on a grid of rewrites with no verbatim-source arm.
why: Without it the grid cannot say whether the rewrite helps or hurts; a run of 17 arms had none.

anchors: comparison needs its own arm with a `task_file` that asks
decision: A remove_skill arm answers only 'without the skill'; a dynamic-workflow comparison needs its own arm whose task_file asks for the Workflow tool, and PREREG.md states the confound that other skills still name the removed one.

evidence.text: 2026-11-05: the user found these missing cells after sealing, each costing a new run dir; the 85-file count is from the frozen plugin checkout.

reopen_if: Removing a skill also scrubs its name from the rest of the frozen plugin, or the bare agent starts using Workflow unprompted.
why: A bare agent never uses the Workflow tool unless its prompt asks, and about 85 files named the executor skill under test after it was removed.

anchors: never report a round as converged from the checklist
decision: Run a fresh defect hunt after every fix round, record which defects each round introduced, and never report a round converged from the checklist score.

evidence.text: 2026-11-06 runs r10/r11, single judge counts, not code-checked; the skill text says so.

reopen_if: A fix round is measured converging (a fresh hunt finding nothing new) on a code-checked count.
why: Fixers raised a 20-item checklist from 2 to 18 and 12 to 19 while a fresh hunt still found 6 to 7 open items per arm, and both fixers wrote the same new flaw.

anchors: Size `deadline_s` from the longest expected arm
decision: Size deadline_s from the longest expected arm (7200 is ample for 12-42 minute arms), not the skeleton's 14400, and set it before seal, since abtest.toml is frozen there.

evidence.text: 2026-11-05 run vnc-r2 and 2026-11-06 (V7 waited 5 pauses, 2.5 h); the rule is _login_lapses in abtest.py, skeleton value abprofile.py deadline_s = 14400.

reopen_if: run stops comparing the arm deadline with the login expiry, or the login refreshes early.
why: run pauses before an arm whose deadline outlasts the login, and the about-8-hour login refreshes only near expiry, so a 4-hour deadline paused runs for hours.

anchors: Commit a `PREREG.md` amendment the moment you write it
decision: Commit a PREREG.md amendment the moment it is written.

evidence.text: 2026-11-05 run vnc-r2: 14 arms refused at zero cost.

reopen_if: run stops checking the sealed inputs for uncommitted changes.
why: run refuses any uncommitted or untracked change under the sealed inputs; an uncommitted amendment failed 14 arms at zero cost.

anchors: plan no more than two long arms per 5-hour window
decision: Before a live run, state its weekly cost (long arms times about 7 points of the 7-day window) and plan at most two long arms per 5-hour window, sizing from the stream's rate_limit_event utilization; a usage-limit notice sets the attempt aside and the arm reruns from scratch.

evidence.text: 2026-11-05 r5 V3 429 at five_hour 100 percent, seven_day 54 to 61 percent over one arm; 2026-11-06 VB2 attempt 1 discarded after 94 min.

reopen_if: run resumes a limit-paused arm instead of setting the attempt aside, or the account's windows change size.
why: One long arm used about 7 points of the 7-day window and about three filled the 5-hour window; a 94-minute attempt was discarded by a limit notice, paying the arm twice.

decision: A --dry-run builds every arm's worktree and runs the full floor, so it is never run beside a live arm, and a killed one leaves arm dirs that the next run sets aside and prune-run removes.

evidence.text: Observed in the plan-executor A/B; behaviour read from abtest.py (dry run skips only the session).

reopen_if: abtest.py gains a dry mode that skips the floor.
why: The skill said 'dry-run first' without saying it costs minutes of CPU per arm and leaves state behind when killed.
